newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan watchdog checking 3 big brokers--JSDA.
newsitem.headline: Japan watchdog checking 3 big brokers--JSDA.

text.p: The vice chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA), Kaname Seki, said on Tuesday that the nation's securities watchdog was checking three major brokerages over possible illegal deals with "sokaiya" racketeers.

Seki also said the brokerages -- Nikko Securities Co Ltd, Daiwa Securities Co Ltd and Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd -- had told the body their internal checks had not so far revealed any illegal deals with sokaiya.
He said the watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), was investigating the three brokerages.

"The three firms have been investigated by the SESC. While they are cooperating with the SESC in the investigation, they have not found any illegal deeds so far," Seki told reporters at the JSDA's regular news conference.

He said the body had questioned Nikko, Daiwa and Yamaichi about allegedly illegal deals on Tuesday morning after Japanese media quoted a lawyer for corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike as saying on Monday that he had told prosecutors that the three brokers conducted illegal discretionary stock deals for him.

Koike is a key figure at the centre of a high-profile racketeer payoff scandal involving Japan's biggest brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd, and one of the nation's top commercial banks, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd.
The lawyer for Koike, Kyuzaburo Hino, confirmed the remarks by Koike in a telephone interview with Reuters on Tuesday. Prosecutors are showing interest in the statements by Koike, he also said.

Discretionary deals by brokerages for their customers are banned by Japan's Securities Law. But such deals would not be subject to any criminal charges unless they could be used by brokers to illegally compensate their clients for stock trading losses, the lawyer said.
